$comment: Single source of truth for every FSharpened pillar. Docs, projects, skills and CI checks are generated from / validated against this file. Edit via an ADR-governed PR (see .agents/skills/add-pillar.md).

pillars.title: Cross-platform abstraction
pillars.summary: Owns every OS-specific behaviour behind interfaces and a capability manifest: file watching, IPC transport, path identity, overlay store, sandboxing, terminal, runtime identity. Nothing else may #if on a platform.

pillars.title: Snapshot / fork / rollback / merge substrate
pillars.summary: Shared statepoint graph used by hot reload, debugging, model canarying, experiment tracking and chaos testing. No component may implement its own checkpointing.

pillars.title: Semantic grounding for agents (MCP + library)
pillars.summary: find / check / types / rename / dead-code plus model-aware queries, exposed as a library and a stdio MCP server. Agents must use it for symbol resolution.

pillars.title: FCS wrapper, warm compiler, per-file cache
pillars.summary: Warm FSharpChecker host, structured diagnostic projection, diagnostic enrichment, onboarding diagnostics, content-addressed per-file typecheck cache exposed as an MSBuild task wrapping CoreCompile.

pillars.title: Structured error and debug logging
pillars.summary: DiagnosticScope CE, Result-centric error pipeline, ILogger integration, Sentry/OTLP bridges. Every error has a typed shape.

pillars.title: OpenTelemetry-native observability
pillars.summary: Compiler Meter/ActivitySource subscription, pipeline instrumentation, dev-loop spans, AOT-safe instrumentation, opt-in privacy-preserving feedback collection, ML instruments.

pillars.title: Curated FSharp.Analyzers.SDK rule set
pillars.summary: File-order, value-restriction, Async/Task, Option/ValueOption, nullability, performance, documentation-coverage, testing-gap and supply-chain rules. Every rule is opt-in and has an RFC with false-positive analysis.

pillars.title: Editor integrations and headless LSP harness
pillars.summary: VS Code companion, VSIX, headless language-server harness, SharpLsp gap closure (upstream-first), statepoint-backed hot-reload sessions.

pillars.title: Build, CI primitives and compiler cache integration
pillars.summary: FAKE / Fun.Build targets, MSBuild cache task integration, `dotnet fsh build --cached`, reference pipelines.

pillars.title: Opt-in language-level gap fillers
pillars.summary: Collections.Immutable, Option (ValueOption-aware), Async/Task bridge, Pipeline. Library-level only: no compiler patches, no FSharp.Core changes, no HKTs.

pillars.title: Unified effect pipeline
pillars.summary: Effect<'T,'E> struct and a single effect { } CE covering async, task, result, option and validation with OTel context. Not algebraic effects at runtime.

pillars.title: AOT-ready, source-generation-free serialization
pillars.summary: System.Text.Json converter factory using analyzer-generated metadata instead of FSharp.Reflection; build-time AOT validation that fails the build with a suggested fix.

pillars.title: F#-aware quality gates
pillars.summary: Complexity computed from the typed AST (match case = decision point), coverage, CRAP, mutation-score gates, baseline-comparison mode.

pillars.title: Functional-first desktop / mobile UI
pillars.summary: MVU wrapper over Avalonia and Fabulous.Avalonia, `dotnet fsh new desktop` template, AOT lane for mobile.

pillars.title: F#-aware debugging and profiling
pillars.summary: DAP proxy over netcoredbg, in-process FCS expression evaluator via ICorDebug, PDB+IL symbol snapshots for hot-reloaded assemblies, profiling bridge.

pillars.title: Type-directed refactorings (MCP first, LSP second)
pillars.summary: rename, extract, inline, move-type, Async to Task, Option to ValueOption; MCP and LSP code actions with identical semantics and test suites.

pillars.title: Composed testing stack
pillars.summary: Unified property facade, AST-native mutation layer where Stryker fails, contract tests from DUs, MVU UI harness, chaos harness with statepoint recovery verification, coverage wrapping.

pillars.title: Composed columnar and tabular interop
pillars.summary: Facade over DuckDB, Flowthru, DataFusionSharp plus a greenfield XParsec-based TOML 1.0.0 parser and streaming CSV.

pillars.title: Supply-chain and artifact governance
pillars.summary: Composes SBOM (dep-scan, SOVA, ShieldedStack), SLSA/Sigstore, lock-file validation (NuGet, CPM and Paket); extends signing and SBOM to model artifacts. Continuous, not release-gate.

pillars.title: Living architecture and fitness functions
pillars.summary: Typed dependency graph from FCS symbol resolution, type-directed fitness-function DSL, generated architecture docs.

pillars.title: Internal specialised models and resilience envelope
pillars.summary: Hyper-specific CDM/APM/ECM/SSM/ATRM models, recursive training pipeline with frozen judges, five-layer deterministic fallback stack, atomic hot-swap via statepoints. The symbolic fallback ships first.

pillars.title: Rust interop: C ABI, cargo and native library resolution
pillars.summary: F# calls Rust through the C ABI only. RID to Rust target-triple table, native library names and runtimes/<rid>/native layout, a no-#if native library resolver, a cargo build plan and cargo metadata reader that wrap cargo, and the ABI conventions (status codes, UTF-8 ownership, panics never cross) every bound Rust library follows.

pillars.title: Capability contracts for fragile ML frameworks
pillars.summary: Every ML framework declares RIDs, dtypes, ops, training/inference support and a stability tier; fallback to ONNX export or ILGPU; version pinning recorded in artifacts.

pillars.title: Hardware abstraction and backend resolver
pillars.summary: Backend registry (Training/Inference/Kernel), capability negotiation, per-task priority-chain resolver and deterministic fallback. CUDA, ROCm/HIP, DirectML, OpenVINO, CoreML, MPS, oneDNN/oneDAL, ILGPU, CPU.

pillars.title: F#-native model definition and training
pillars.summary: model { } and training { } CEs, DU architectures, nested-AD combinators, elastic distributed training via statepoint rollback.

pillars.title: Typed, lineage-tracked ML data pipelines
pillars.summary: Typed frames with provenance DAG, schema and drift validation, reproducible splits seeded from the statepoint graph, streaming.

pillars.title: Experiment tracking, search and AutoML
pillars.summary: Local-first tracker where every run is a statepoint; typed search { } CE (random, Bayesian, Hyperband, PBT); AutoML wrapper; notebook integration. Genuinely greenfield.

pillars.title: Signed model registry and promotion
pillars.summary: Content-addressed store, staged promotion with frozen-judge gates, ONNX export with six-RID AOT validation, signed model cards. Genuinely greenfield.

pillars.title: Inference runtime, drift response, shadow deploy
pillars.summary: ONNX-first runtime with batching and warm-up, Giraffe integration, drift detection, shadow traffic, automatic rollback to prior artifact.

tools.title: dotnet fsh command line
tools.summary: init, watch, doctor, analyze, quality, explain, refactor, mutate, build --cached, sign, architecture check, new desktop.

tools.title: Warm compiler and statepoint-backed hot reload
tools.summary: Warm FSharpChecker daemon over IPC; Harmony-backed patching now, FCS-native hot reload session when upstream lands.

invariants.text: No component may be platform-privileged. Every component is platform-neutral or first-class on every Tier 1 platform; platform behaviour lives only in FSharpened.Platform.
Every maintainable action is a documented, numbered, repeatable procedure (a skill). No skill means not maintainable.
No model is promoted without a frozen judge, a canary statepoint and an automatic rollback path.
No pillar may degrade another pillar's platform support. The six-RID matrix enforces this.
No component may implement its own checkpointing, symbol resolution or model artifact loading. Statepoints, Semantic and Models are the only sanctioned implementations.
No model artifact may be promoted without a signed model card, a frozen-judge report and a canary statepoint.
No ML component may bypass the statepoint runtime for checkpointing, Telemetry for instrumentation, or Security for artifact signing.
No ML component may hard-code a backend. All training, inference and kernel execution routes through FSharpened.ML.Hardware.Resolver.
No backend is promoted without a per-RID initialisation smoke test and a deterministic fallback test.
No ML component may depend directly on TorchSharp, DiffSharp or Furnace without going through FSharpened.ML.Portability.
No security or testing component may reimplement what an existing .NET/F# tool provides. Composition is the default; exceptions need an ADR.
No agent may proceed past a disagreement without invoking the conflict-resolution protocol.
No component may regress beyond its documented performance budget without an ADR that accepts the regression.
No dependency may be added without a license entry and an upstream-policy assessment.
